---
title: "Derive outcomes, comorbidities, and costs"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
---

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The examples use invented data.

## Add outcomes and score comorbidities

> The NIS has no diagnosis-level present-on-admission fields (`DXPOA`).
> The default Elixhauser method assumes diagnoses were present on admission.
> That assumption differs from the AHRQ Refined method with known POA.
> Document it if you use these scores for risk adjustment.

```{r outcomes}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020))
outcomes <- nis |> nis_outcomes()
outcomes |> select(in_hospital_death, los_days) |> head() |> collect()
```

`DIED` defines in-hospital death. `DISPUNIFORM` describes where the patient
went at discharge. `los_days` comes from `LOS`. Keep all three source fields
when calling `nis_outcomes()`.

```{r comorbidity}
scored <- outcomes |> nis_comorbidity(method = "charlson_quan2005")
scored |> select(starts_with("cmrb_")) |> head(3) |> collect()
```

Score before `nis_design()` while the diagnosis slots are available and
DuckDB can still apply the mappings. Choose the method and code system for
your study period. The Charlson example needs `medicalcoder`.
The bundled `"elixhauser_ahrq2027"` method has no `medicalcoder` dependency.

## Estimate costs in a common dollar year

```{r cost}
charges <- outcomes |> select(YEAR, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS) |> collect()
costs <- nis_cost(charges, dollars = 2020)
nis_cost_provenance(costs)
costs |>
  transmute(YEAR, billed = TOTCHG, charges_adj,
            cost_at_discharge = TOTCHG * CCR_NIS, cost_adj) |>
  head()
```

Join the year-specific HCUP cost-to-charge ratio before estimating costs
if the data lack `CCR_NIS`. `charges_adj` is the adjusted billed amount.
`cost_adj` applies the hospital ratio to estimate costs. Missing or invalid
ratios yield missing costs. CPI-U tracks general consumer price inflation.
It does not track hospital-specific input prices. When comparing with a
legacy result, check its charge field, CCR source, price index, and
dollar year. Keep the provenance alongside both cost and charge results.
[Years and coding eras](years-and-eras.html)

If `nis_design()` keeps both `TOTCHG` and `CCR_NIS`, it adds `charges_adj` and
`cost_adj` in dollars of the latest included year by default. Use `nis_cost()`
to set a common dollar year across separate analyses and retain the
provenance with your results.
